title: automated-canary-eval-harness-and-rollback-for-config-or-model-changes
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Summary:
Implement an automated canary evaluation harness that runs whenever a model version or inference config changes. The harness must gate Canary and A/B rollouts with quantifiable quality checks and trigger an automatic rollback when thresholds are breached. Goals are to: reduce undetected regressions in production, make rollouts predictable/observable, and eliminate manual rollback toil for common regressions.

Scope:
- New evaluation runner that executes lightweight, production-proximal evals against live canary traffic (sampled) and against offline holdout prompt sets.
- Policy engine for gating that supports: weighted canary ramps (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%), A/B splits (50/50), and time/windows-based checks.
- Pre-defined metric suite: primary model-quality metric (task-specific: e.g., exact-match or slot-F1), hallucination-rate (model asserts unverifiable facts), toxic-content-rate, latency P95, token-cost delta, and downstream regression tests (business-specific prompts).
- Auto-rollback rules: configurable rules that can trigger immediate rollback and alerting when breached. Example defaults: primary metric relative drop > 5% over baseline (min sample size 1k), hallucination-rate absolute increase > 2 percentage points, latency P95 increase > 30% absolute or > 2x baseline, or critical downstream tests fail.
- Integrations with Console: surface canary dashboard, historical comparisons, and one-click manual override to promote or abort.
- Auditing: persist evaluation snapshots and decision logs to allow postmortems and MLREPRO.

Acceptance criteria:
- Harness runs automatically when any of {model.version, quantization, batch_size, KV cache policy, temperature, sampling topology} are changed in a rollout request.
- For a 1% canary traffic run using a synthetic+live prompt sample, the harness produces metric report within 10 minutes and policy decision within 15 minutes.
- If a threshold is breached, the system issues a rollback to last stable version and posts a standardized incident message to #deploy-alerts and creates a rollback ticket (automatically linked).
- Operators can adjust thresholds per-customer and per-project via Console feature flags.

Design notes & trade-offs:
- Sampling: we will use a risk-balanced sampling strategy that mixes a small slice of live traffic (to detect real-world regressions) with synthetic/regression prompt sets (to detect targeted regressions) to keep privacy and cost constraints.
- Latency of decision vs. statistical confidence: shorter windows give faster feedback but higher false positives. We choose an initial conservative sample and require multiple signals before auto-rollback for low-impact metrics; primary-model-quality and critical downstream tests can trigger immediate rollback.
- Where to run evaluations: lightweight evals run in a chilled canary pool (lower-cost instances) while heavier offline evals run in Evals fleet.
- Revert vs. degrade: some regressions are tolerable (small latency increases) and should trigger throttling (reduce canary weight) rather than full rollback. Implement 2-tier actions: throttle -> pause -> rollback.

Implementation plan (high-level):
1) Build an Eval Runner service endpoint that accepts: rollout_id, policy_id, sample_id, baseline_metrics_ref. Returns post-eval metric bundle. (Owner: Asha)
2) Extend Router to support canary fraction labels and mirror sampling for eval capture. (Owner: Marco)
3) Policy Engine: evaluate rules, maintain state machine for ramp, and perform automated actions (throttle/promote/rollback). (Owner: Priya)
4) Console UI: canary dashboard + manual controls + thresholds editing. (Owner: Design/Console PM)
5) Alerts/Logging: integrate with PagerDuty/Slack and persist to S3/BigQuery for audit. (Owner: Infra)
6) E2E test harness and chaos tests that simulate regressions. (Owner: SRE)

Telemetry & metrics to collect:
- primary_metric.current, primary_metric.baseline, primary_metric.delta_pct
- hallucination_rate.current, toxic_rate.current
- latency_p95.current, latency_p50.current
- token_cost.delta_per_k_tokens
- decision_latency_seconds (time from canary start to policy decision)
- sample_size_total

Runbook excerpt (automatic rollback):
- If policy engine returns ROLLBACK: immediately route traffic to previous stable model version and mark rollout as aborted. Post message to #deploy-alerts with link to evaluation artifact. Create ENG-rollback-<timestamp> ticket.
- If policy engine returns THROTTLE: reduce canary weight to previous step and re-evaluate after 30 minutes.

Security & privacy considerations:
- Live traffic sampling must strip PII before being stored for offline evaluation; follow existing private-deployment KMS rules.
- Evaluation artifacts stored with access controls and 90-day retention by default.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for policy logic and metric calculations.
- Integration test driving a small canary rollout in staging with synthetic regressions injected to verify throttle vs rollback behaviors.
- Load test to ensure Eval Runner can handle 100 concurrent canaries without impacting production latency.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (staging): core engine + simple policy, test on internal models only.
- Phase 2 (alpha): opt-in for a small set of customers using Dedicated.
- Phase 3 (GA): enable for all Hosted rollouts with default thresholds and opt-out.
